name: acolyte
desc: Acolytes are junior members of a clergy, usually answerable to a priest. They perform a variety of functions in a temple and are granted minor spellcasting power by their deities.

special_abilities.name: spellcasting
special_abilities.desc:
The acolyte is a 1st-level spellcaster. Its spellcasting ability is Wisdom (spell save DC 12, +4 to hit with spell attacks). The acolyte has following cleric spells prepared:

- Cantrips (at will): light, sacred flame, thaumaturgy
- 1st level (3 slots): bless, cure wounds, sanctuary

actions.name: club
actions.desc: Melee Weapon Attack: +2 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. Hit: 2 (1d4) bludgeoning damage.

lore:
The Acolyte is a hollowed vessel, a grim remnant haunting the salt-crusted ruins of the Sunken Cathedrals and sun-bleached cloisters of the High Wastes. Though they appear as stooped, robed figures, do not be deceived by their stillness. They do not breathe; they wait.

Their predation is a subtle cruelty. They emit a low, harmonic hum that mimics the vibration of ancient liturgy, drawing the weary and the faithful into their orbit. Once a victim kneels in shared supplication, the Acolyte’s jaw unhinges with a sickening crack, siphoning the very spirit from the victim’s lungs. They do not consume flesh, but "sanctity"—leaving behind a husk as cold and empty as the stone they inhabit.

Local folklore names them the *Echoes of the Unanswered*. Mothers warn children that to pray in a ruined house is to invite a guest who will never leave. To encounter an Acolyte is to witness the terrifying persistence of a faith that has outlived its god, transformed into a hunger that knows no end. Such is the fate of those who seek divinity in the dark.
